I am applying for a no plan check construction permit in order to make repairs to the upper lateral of my sewer line. I have already applied for a sewer permit which relates to the repairs downstream of the sewer cleanout. I have been informed that I also need to apply for a construction permit for the repairs upstream of the sewer cleanout going into my home. In essence I am replacing the majority of the upper lateral of the sewer for my home. The upstairs bathroom was modernized by a previous owner with ABS lines that tie into a cast iron stack. That cast iron stack, and everything downstream of it up to the cleanout will be replaced (that is the section relevant to this construction permit, the section from the cleanout to where the repairs will be tied into the old cast iron relates to the sewer permit). This will involve removing the concrete pavers using a concrete saw, and then digging down by hand approximately a foot to reach the old cast iron, removing it. adding a bed of gravel, and then installing the new schedule 40 ABS piping& fittings. There are three main drainage points which are shown on the engineering drawing, a drain for the downstairs toilet, the main stack, and a drain for the upstairs kitchen sink/downstairs laundry room sink.
